interface.name: otto_surface_style_manager_v1

description.summary: declarative animations and compositing for Wayland

interface.description:
Otto surface style protocol provides declarative animations and advanced compositing features. Clients can augment wayland surfaces with animations and visual effects by creating style surfaces. Animations are defined using transaction-based property changes.
The compositor manages all animation state and execution, providing smooth, GPU-accelerated animations with minimal IPC overhead.

request.name: get_surface_style

description.summary: create a style surface to augment an existing surface

request.description: Create a style surface that augments an existing wl_surface with additional compositing and animation capabilities. The style surface is purely decorative and does not have its own wl_surface or role. It can augment any surface type (for example xdg_toplevel, xdg_popup, etc.) with effects like blur, shadows, animations, and blend modes.

request.name: begin_transaction
request.description: Start a transaction context. All property changes made to style surfaces within this transaction are applied together when the transaction is committed. If a duration is set, they animate together. Transactions are scoped per client connection.

request.name: create_timing_function

description.summary: create a timing function for animations

request.description: Create a timing function that defines how animated values interpolate over time. Can be configured as bezier curves, springs, or presets.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request destroys the manager object. Style surfaces, transactions, and timing functions created through this instance are not affected.

interface.name: otto_surface_style_v1
interface.description:
A style surface augments a wl_surface and provides additional compositing and animation capabilities. It can have transforms, effects, and visual properties like shadows, blur, and corner radius.
Property changes made within a transaction animate when a duration is set. If no duration is set, they apply when the transaction is committed. Property changes made outside a transaction apply immediately.

enum.name: z_order

description.summary: surface z-order relative to surface content

enum.description: Defines where the style surface appears in the stacking order relative to the parent window's content.

request.name: set_z_order
request.description: Set whether this style surface renders above or below the parent window's surface content. Default is above_surface.

request.name: set_position
request.description: Set the style surface's position in its parent's coordinate space. If called within a transaction, animates from the current position.

request.name: set_z_position
request.description: Set the style surface's position on the z-axis for 3D positioning. Surfaces with higher z values appear in front.

request.name: set_size
request.description: Set the style surface's size. The position is relative to the anchor point.

request.name: set_scale
request.description: Set the style surface's scale factors. Applied relative to the anchor point.

request.name: set_rotation
request.description: Set the style surface's rotation in radians around the z-axis. Applied relative to the anchor point.

request.name: set_anchor_point
request.description: Set the point within the style surface that transforms are applied relative to. Expressed as normalized coordinates (0.0 to 1.0) where (0,0) is top-left and (1,1) is bottom-right. Default is (0.5, 0.5) - center.

request.name: set_transform
request.description: Set a full 4x4 transformation matrix for advanced 3D effects. For simple transforms, prefer the individual transform methods.

request.name: set_opacity
request.description: Set the style surface's opacity.

request.name: set_background_color
request.description: Set the style surface's background color. Colors are in sRGB color space.

request.name: set_corner_radius
request.description: Set the corner radius for rounded corners. The surface content is clipped to this shape.

enum.name: output_placement

description.summary: how a surface's position is resolved

enum.description: Positions set through set_position are relative to the surface's parent. A surface that has to sit in a fixed place on the display cannot express that: a client is never told where its own window is, so it cannot work out the offset. This enum lets it ask the compositor, which knows both, to resolve the position against the output instead.

entry.name: parent
entry.summary: position is relative to the parent (default)

entry.name: output_centered
entry.summary: centred on the output the surface is shown on

request.name: set_output_placement

description.summary: centre the surface on its output (animatable)

request.description:
WARNING: this is the wrong request for a subsurface. It moves the style surface's own layer, which carries only what the compositor paints — background, blur, shadow, rounded corners. A subsurface's buffer is placed by wl_subsurface.set_position, which the compositor does not touch, so centring the layer leaves a card's frame in the middle of the display and its contents back over the window. Use request_output_frame and set the position yourself: that moves both. This request is only appropriate for a surface whose layer carries its pixels.
Resolve this surface's position against the output rather than against its parent. With output_centered the compositor keeps the surface centred on the output it is shown on, following it across moves of the parent, resizes of the surface, and changes of output or mode.
Setting the placement back to parent restores the position last set through set_position.

request.name: request_output_frame

description.summary: ask where this surface's output is

request.description:
Ask the compositor for the geometry of the output this surface is shown on, answered with an output_frame event.
A client is never told where its own window sits, so it cannot place a surface anywhere but relative to its parent. This is the missing piece: the answer is expressed in the same coordinates the client already passes to set_position, so centring a surface on the display is arithmetic the client can do itself — and, unlike having the compositor move the surface, it moves the client's own content with it.
The rect is the output's *usable* area: what is left after the dock and any layer-shell exclusive zones have taken their share. A surface centred in it sits where the eye expects, rather than low on the screen because the dock took the bottom.
The answer is a snapshot. A client that cares about the surface moving between outputs, the mode changing, or the reserved areas changing, asks again.

event.name: output_frame
event.description:
The output this surface is shown on, relative to this surface's parent, in the same physical pixels this interface's set_position and set_size use. Centring is then x + (width - surface_width) / 2.
Mind the units when the surface is a subsurface: this interface works in physical pixels, while wl_subsurface.set_position works in surface-local coordinates. Divide by the surface's scale before passing a position to wl_subsurface, or the surface lands at the scale factor times the offset you meant.
Sent in reply to request_output_frame.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: output's left edge, in this surface's coordinates

arg.name: y
arg.summary: output's top edge, in this surface's coordinates

event.name: desktop_frame

description.summary: where this surface is on the desktop

event.description:
Where the compositor is drawing this surface, in the desktop's own coordinate space — the space output positions and pointer positions are in, with its origin at the top-left of the desktop rather than of any one output.
A client is never told where its window is, which is fine for drawing and wrong for anything that has to answer "what is at this point on the screen". An assistive technology reads the desktop by position: it asks an application what is at a screen coordinate, and it draws the focus highlight and moves the magnifier from the rects the application gives back. A window that answers in its own coordinates claims the rectangle at the same offset from the desktop's origin — which belongs to whatever is drawn in the top-left corner of the screen, and usually not to the window at all.
Sent when the surface is first drawn and whenever the rect changes: the window moving, the workspace scrolling under it, the output moving, a mode or a scale change. A client that only draws can ignore it.
In physical pixels, like everything else on this interface. Divide by the surface's scale for the logical pixels an assistive technology works in.
This is where the compositor draws the surface itself. It is not affected by the window overview, which draws scaled-down copies rather than moving the windows: a window in the overview keeps reporting where it will be when the overview closes, and the shell describes the overview itself.

request.name: set_output_relative_size

description.summary: size the surface as a fraction of its output (animatable)

request.description:
Set the surface's size as a fraction of the output it is shown on — 0.5 being half the output's width or height. The compositor recomputes it when the output or its mode changes, so a panel keeps its share of the display without the client tracking modes.
Fractions are clamped to 0.0 - 1.0. A fraction of 0.0 leaves that axis to whatever set_size last established, so one axis can be output relative while the other is fixed.
The minimums are a floor in surface-local pixels, applied after the fraction: a panel that is a sensible share of a large display is useless on a small one, and this is where that is expressed. Pass 0.0 for no floor.
Like set_size, this marks the bounds as client owned.

request.name: set_border
request.description: Set the style surface's border. The border is drawn inside the surface bounds.

request.name: set_shadow
request.description: Set the style surface's drop shadow effect.

enum.name: blend_mode
enum.description: Defines how this surface blends with content behind it.

enum.name: visibility
enum.description: Defines whether the style surface is rendered.

enum.name: clip_mode
enum.description: Defines whether content is clipped to the style surface bounds. Used by both set_masks_to_bounds (the surface's own content) and set_clip_children (the surface's descendant surfaces).

enum.name: contents_gravity

description.summary: how the surface buffer is rendered within layer bounds

enum.description: Controls how the Wayland buffer texture is positioned and scaled within the layer bounds. Mirrors Core Animation's contentsGravity. When the layer bounds differ from the buffer size (e.g. during a size animation), this determines the rendering strategy.

entry.name: resize_aspect
entry.summary: scale uniformly to fit, preserving aspect ratio (letterbox)

entry.name: resize_aspect_fill
entry.summary: scale uniformly to fill, preserving aspect ratio (crop)

entry.name: center
entry.summary: natural buffer size, centred in bounds

entry.name: top_left
entry.summary: natural buffer size, pinned to top-left

entry.name: top_right
entry.summary: natural buffer size, pinned to top-right

request.name: set_blend_mode
request.description: Set how this surface blends with content behind it. When set to background_blur, the content behind this surface is blurred before the surface is composited on top.

request.name: set_hidden
request.description: Set the style surface visibility state.

request.name: set_masks_to_bounds
request.description: Set whether content is clipped to this surface's bounds.

request.name: set_clip_children
request.description:
Set whether the surfaces descending from the augmented wl_surface — its subsurfaces, and their subsurfaces in turn — are clipped to this surface's style bounds. Content of a descendant that falls outside the bounds is not rendered.
This is independent of set_masks_to_bounds: a surface can clip its children while leaving its own content unclipped, and the other way round. The two requests do not imply each other and neither one overrides the other.
The clipping rectangle is the style node's size, as set by set_size, together with the corner radius set by set_corner_radius. That size is the client's to choose and need not match the surface's buffer size, so a client can keep a small fixed viewport while a subsurface behind it carries a much larger buffer that is moved around by set_position — the usual way to build a scrolling view whose cropping the compositor performs.
Changes take effect immediately, or with the enclosing transaction when one is active. The default is disabled.

request.name: set_contents_gravity

description.summary: set how the buffer texture is rendered within layer bounds

request.description: Set the contents gravity, controlling how the Wayland buffer texture is positioned and scaled when the layer bounds differ from the buffer size. The default is resize (stretch to fill). Changes take effect immediately and are not animatable.

request.name: cancel_animation
request.description: Cancel a specific animation by its key. The animated property remains at its current value. The key is the request name for the animated property (for example set_opacity or set_position).

request.name: cancel_all_animations
request.description: Cancel all animations on this surface. Properties remain at their current animated values.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy this style surface and remove all associated animations and effects from the augmented wl_surface.

interface.name: otto_style_transaction_v1
interface.description: A transaction groups style property changes that should be applied together. While a transaction is active, changes made to style surfaces are collected and applied atomically when the transaction is committed. If a duration is set, the compositor animates the transition to the new values.

request.name: set_duration
request.description: Set the duration for all animations in this transaction. If not set, property changes apply immediately without animation.

request.name: set_timing_function
request.description: Set the timing function that controls how animated values interpolate. If not set, defaults to linear interpolation.

request.name: set_delay
request.description: Set a delay before animations in this transaction start executing.

request.name: enable_completion_event
request.description: Request that a completion event be sent when all animations in this transaction finish executing.

request.name: commit
request.description: Commit all pending property changes. If a duration is set, changes will animate. Otherwise they apply immediately.

event.name: completed
event.description: Sent when all animations in this transaction have finished executing. Only sent if enable_completion_event was called before commit.

request.name: cancel
request.description: Cancel and destroy this transaction object. If not yet committed, all pending changes are discarded.

interface.name: otto_timing_function_v1
interface.description: Defines how animated property values interpolate over time. Can be configured as preset curves, custom bezier curves, or spring physics.

request.name: set_bezier
request.description: Define a custom cubic bezier curve. The curve starts at (0,0) and ends at (1,1). This request sets the two middle control points.

request.name: set_spring

description.summary: spring-based timing with duration and bounce

request.description: Configure spring physics timing using bounce and velocity parameters. The spring is tuned to settle within the transaction's duration with the specified bounce characteristic. Use this when you want spring-like motion but need to respect a specific duration.

arg.name: bounce
arg.summary: bounce amount (0.0 = no bounce, 1.0 = maximum bounce)

request.name: set_spring_stiffness_damping
request.description: Configure spring physics timing using stiffness and damping parameters. This creates natural, interruptible physics-based animations. The spring runs until it naturally settles based on its physical properties. Transaction duration is ignored for this spring type.
